module.title: Starters and leavers: preserve the employment identity
module.goal: Build a dated payroll handoff and distinguish same-year from later-year post-cessation reporting.
module.scope: Irish employment-lifecycle reporting foundation. No live RPN request, personal identifiers, termination entitlement or tax-rate calculation. Exceptional cases and actual software workflows need review.

sections.title: 1. Build the starter record
paragraphs: Original starter checklist: approved commencement date, correct employee and employment identity, pay terms, payroll period and current RPN process. Use fictional identifiers during training. Resolve a missing or conflicting record through the authorised onboarding process rather than borrowing another employee’s settings.

Revenue publishes current RPN request guidance. Treat the RPN and approved employee inputs as records to verify, not values to invent from a prior payslip. This exercise does not determine a new employee’s credits, cut-offs or tax treatment.
sections.supportPt: Confirme identidade, início e RPN. Nunca copie parâmetros de outro funcionário.

sections.title: 2. Record the actual leaving date
paragraphs: Revenue requires the leaving date on the final payroll submission to notify cessation. The leaving date and payment date are separate facts; they can differ.

Original case: employment ends on 31 August 2026 and a final approved payment is made on 4 September. Keep both dates. Do not change the leaving date to 4 September merely to make the fields look consistent. Verify the final inputs and submission details before approval.
sections.supportPt: Data de saída e data de pagamento são fatos distintos. Não altere uma para coincidir com a outra.

sections.title: 3. Handle a later payment
paragraphs: Revenue’s post-cessation guidance distinguishes a payment in the cessation year from one in a later year. Both retain the original employment ID and cessation date and use the actual later payment date. For a later-year payment, the guidance calls for a new RPN request without a commencement date.

Original decision exercise: a bonus relating to the ceased employment is paid in January 2027 after an August 2026 departure. Do not create a fictional rehire to process it. Record the actual facts and use the applicable out-of-year route. The bonus amount and tax calculation are deliberately not supplied.
sections.supportPt: Pagamento posterior não cria recontratação. Preserve o vínculo original e use o procedimento do ano correto.

sections.title: 4. Review the handoff
paragraphs: Original handoff note: record who confirmed cessation, who approved the later payment, which RPN route applies, the original identity and dates, and how submission acceptance will be checked. Keep unresolved entitlement or rate questions open for the responsible reviewer.

Before closing the case, compare payroll and submission records. Do not promise a refund or net amount from dates alone. The lifecycle checklist controls identity and timing; it is not a termination-pay calculator.
sections.supportPt: Confira vínculo, datas, aprovação e aceite. As datas não permitem calcular o líquido.

caseStudy.title: Starters and leavers: preserve the employment identity — applied case
scenario: Fictional employment ID TRAIN-6 ceased on 31 August 2026.
Final approved payment made 4 September 2026. A later approved bonus will be paid 15 January 2027 for that ceased employment.
No rehire occurred. Tax calculation and bonus amount are outside the case.
caseStudy.task: Prepare the identity/date handoff for the later bonus and identify the applicable RPN route.
hints: Compare payment year with cessation year.
Do not create a new commencement.
caseStudy.modelAnswer: Use the out-of-year post-cessation route: request a new RPN without a commencement date, retain original employment ID TRAIN-6 and cessation 31 August 2026, and report actual payment date 15 January 2027. Keep approval and submission acceptance evidence. Do not invent a rehire or a net bonus amount.
reviewChecks: No invented commencement or tax amount.
caseStudy.transfer: For a bonus paid in September 2026 instead, identify the same-year route from the source rather than carrying over every out-of-year step.

practiceExercises.question: An employee leaves 30 June and is paid 7 July. Which date describes leaving?
practiceExercises.explanation: Dates can differ without either being wrong.

practiceExercises.question: A same-year post-cessation payment is due. What identity facts should remain?
practiceExercises.answer: Original employment ID and cessation date; use the actual payment date and the same-year RPN process.
practiceExercises.explanation: A later payment does not itself reopen employment.

practiceExercises.question: A starter lacks verified identity data. Should you copy a similar employee’s tax settings?
practiceExercises.answer: No. Resolve the identity and applicable RPN workflow through authorised onboarding.
practiceExercises.explanation: Another employee’s record is not evidence for this person.

professorGuide.opening: Ask the learner to put cessation and payment dates on a timeline.
professorGuide.whenCorrect: Move the bonus payment to the cessation year and ask what changes and what remains fixed.
professorGuide.whenUncertain: Ask which supplied fact is missing or unclear. Offer the first case hint, then invite another attempt.
professorGuide.whenMisconception: If they create a rehire, ask which supplied event establishes a new employment; there is none.
professorGuide.whenSelfCorrected: Use the corrected answer, not the abandoned phrase, as the current response. Ask one transfer question.
professorGuide.whenAskedForAnswer: Provide a concise explanation and one worked step; invite an optional fresh attempt without claiming independent mastery.
professorGuide.evidenceBoundary: Use only actual session evidence if this guide is separately integrated. Never consume local drafts or checkpoint results. Do not infer pronunciation/acoustic fluency from text, technical mastery from a phrase, or a CEFR level from one task.

assessmentBoundaries: Authored answer keys and guide branches are expectations, not model results or learner evidence.
